extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants interacting with the Korean patent system (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) official Patent Examination Guidelines (English edition) describing legal, procedural and substantive criteria examiners use to examine patent applications and guidance applicants can use when filing or amending applications in Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to conduct patent-related proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal capacity rules determining who may file an application or conduct patent-related proceedings (e.g., minors under guardianship must be represented; representatives of unincorporated associations may act in the association's name; overseas residents must use a patent administrator with domicile or place of business in Korea unless sojourning in Korea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Articles such as Article 3 (Legal Capacity of Minors, etc.), Article 4 (Unincorporated Associations), Article 5 (Patent Administrators for Overseas Residents) and related explanatory text describing limits and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents and representation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on who may act as legal representative, contractual representative, patent administrator, appointment or replacement of representative, and other provisions for representation in patent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedural requirements for appointment/replacement, scope of authority, distinctions among legal representative, contractual representative, patent administrator and administrative formalities for representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and extension of periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of procedural periods, rules for their calculation, and grounds/methods for extension of periods relevant to patent prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes calculation conventions, types of periods (filing, response, priority, etc.), and extension/restore procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceeding and return of documents (formalities examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles for formalities examination and grounds and procedures for invalidation of proceedings, revocation of invalidation, return of documents, subsequent completion, and restoration of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out formal defects that may invalidate proceedings and how applicants can remedy or request revocation of invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation and resumption of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing discontinuation of patent proceedings and conditions/procedures for continuation or resumption of proceedings and succession of effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural criteria include causes of discontinuation, notice requirements, and methods to resume or continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and service of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures for submission of documents to KIPO and methods/requirements for service of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes acceptable submission formats, signatures, translations, and service rules (how notices are served and effective dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment, reduction and refund of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for payment of patent fees, provisions for fee reduction, and procedures for refunding patent or official fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains timing, forms of payment, eligibility for reductions (e.g., small entity), and refund conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection, confidentiality and handling of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on inspection of application documents, prohibition of removal or public disclosure, referencing documents, and offenses for divulging confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers who may inspect, restrictions on access, citation procedures, and criminal/administrative protections for confidential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application formal/essential elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for a valid patent application including inventor identification, successor in title, protection of legitimate holder, and references required in filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies documentary requirements and evidentiary proof for inventor and ownership claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cover sheet requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required contents and formalities for the application cover sheet (bibliographic data and declarations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out what metadata must be present on filing (applicant, inventor, title, priority claims, agent, signatures, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the abstract part of the application (concise summary of invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on length, content (technical field, gist of invention), and how it is used for publication/searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive requirements for the specification including structure and content of the description of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates to enablement, how to disclose embodiments, best mode (where applicable), and required elements for clear disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and substantive requirements for drawings submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when drawings are necessary, required views, scales, legends, and consistency with the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed invention must be enabled — the description must enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention as of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance in Chapter 3 (Description of Invention) and relates to sufficiency of disclosure and what level of detail is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description method requirements and background art description
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular requirements on how the invention and background art should be described, including what background must be acknowledged and how to present prior art in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes instructions regarding avoiding adding new matter, proper citation of background, and characterization of technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: recognition and support by description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description; claims should be drafted so that the invention is recognized and supported by the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sections 'Recognition of Invention', 'Claims supported by Description of Invention' and examples of unacceptable claim-scope not supported by disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should provide a clear and concise statement of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on clarity, definiteness, avoiding ambiguous terms, and meeting statutory claim form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters necessary for specification of invention (claim content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify matters deemed necessary for the specification of the invention that must be included in claims or described sufficiently in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses essential technical features that must be claimed or disclosed to properly define the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting requirements and deferral of submission of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and best practices for drafting claims and the system allowing deferral of submission of claims in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains concrete drafting rules and the special procedure for deferring claims under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and method for determining unity of invention — whether claims form a single general inventive concept or require divisional filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains general considerations, determination criteria, examples, special cases, and examiner instructions for assessing unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism-related application requirements (deposit system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for patent applications involving microorganisms: deposit requirements, procedures, instructions on examination concerning biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers deposit of biological materials, accession information, and how such deposits interact with enablement and written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the invention be industrially applicable — statutory inventions and what constitutes industrial applicability; inventions that are industrially inapplicable are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the purport and tests for industrial applicability and lists types of inventions that may be considered inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 29 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty requirement and methods for determining whether the claimed invention is new in light of prior art and disclosure exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes understanding of provisions, determination methods, disclosure exceptions and how to treat data-only differences and inherent disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness) — general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and methods for determining inventive step: define closest prior art, person having ordinary skill in the art, problems solved by the invention, and how to reason to assess obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains general principles and concrete methods of determining inventive step (see Chapter 3, Part III); examiners should evaluate whether reasoning from prior art and common general knowledge would lead to the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step — treatment of combination from different fields
rubrics_metrics.description: When combining methods or means used in different fields or applying them to another field, such combination is usually considered within ordinary creative activity of a person skilled in the art; inventive step is not affirmatively inferred unless there exist special circumstances (e.g., remarkably advantageous effects) or technical difficulty (teaching-away).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software/IT examples emphasized: combinations across fields are ordinarily expected unless there is a blocking factor or remarkable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step — role of closest prior art and common general knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should base assessment on the closest prior art (including well-known/commonly used art) and the common general knowledge; reasoning can come from various aspects (selection of optimal material, design modification, mere aggregation, or whether prior art discloses motivation to arrive at the claimed invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reasoning from these sources makes the claimed invention obvious, inventive step should be denied; otherwise it should not be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step — problems to be solved by computer-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: In computer-related inventions, problems such as 'improve the level of decision by using AI' or 'make input-operation easier by using GUI' are typical; assessment of inventive step should take these generally known problems into account as of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must consider which problems are generic/common to the field and not automatically confer inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of person having ordinary skill in the art (software/computer-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer-related inventions, a person skilled in the art is expected to have common general knowledge both in the applied software field and computer technology; to use ordinary technical means for R&D; to exercise ordinary creative activity in design modification; and to comprehend the state of the art as of filing. It is often appropriate to consider 'a person skilled in the art' as a group of persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider breadth of skills (applied field + systematization/computer tech) when evaluating obviousness and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of ordinary creative activity (computer-related inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated examples of activities within ordinary creativity expected of a person skilled in the art: (1) application to other fields, (2) addition of commonly known means or replacement by equivalent, (3) implementing hardware functions by software, (4) systematization of human transactions by routine system analysis/design, (5) reproduction of known events in virtual space by routine methods, (6) design modification based on known facts/customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains multiple concrete examples showing when claimed differences are routine and thus not inventive (e.g., applying file retrieval means to a different domain is ordinary creativity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of commercial success as secondary consideration for inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial success (or equivalent) may be referenced to affirmatively infer inventive step, but only where it is convincingly attributable to the feature of the claimed invention rather than other causes (marketing, advertising).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must assert/prove causal link between success and claimed technical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when difference is only in data contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the only difference between the claimed invention and the closest prior art is data contents, novelty or inventive step cannot be affirmatively inferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that merely changing the subject-matter of the data (e.g., student vs racehorse records) does not create novelty when structure/processing is the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording program/data on a computer-readable storage medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the difference from prior art is within ordinary creativity, inventive step cannot be inferred merely by adding the limitation 'recording a program or data on a computer-readable storage medium'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding a medium limitation that is inherent or routine does not confer inventiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims or inventions defined only by an information transmission medium
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claimed invention is specified only by a feature inherent to an information transmission medium (e.g., 'a medium which can transmit certain information'), the claimed invention lacks novelty or inventive step because such a function is inherent to ordinary communication networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that claiming merely a medium that transmits a program or certain digital information does not distinguish product features from prior art and is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged concept of novelty (Article 29(3) etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special statutory provision expanding the concept of novelty in particular situations; conditions and exceptions for applying the enlarged concept and method for determination of identicalness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of Article 29(3)/(4) and exceptions for international applications and identicalness determination are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file rule and application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the first-to-file principle (Article 36 purport) including requirements for application, examination methods, and instructions for examiners on applying first-to-file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains timing and priority consequences under the first-to-file system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable inventions (Article 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of inventions excluded from patentability under statutory provisions and the purport of Article 32 with examples of unpatentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on identifying statutory exclusions and applying the statute to concrete cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible amendment and refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing voluntary amendments and amendments in reply to office actions, amendments necessitated by other amendments or reexamination, requirements and reasons for refusing to enter an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Articles 47, 51, 63 and detailed examination methods and cautions when refusing entry of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: General examination procedure and examiner duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of examination process: designation of examiner, classification, laying open, request/start of examination, processing deadlines, and general principles for law application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for examiner workflow, deadlines, and legal application principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for prior art: procedures and post-search measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for searching prior art: pre-search steps, search procedure, measures after searching, and use of authorized prior art search institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies search scope, documentation of search, and what to do based on search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination process: understanding invention, prior art review, notices and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination activities including understanding the invention, reviewing prior art documents, issuing notice of grounds for rejection, instructions for written argument, conducting interviews, additional searches, and decision to grant or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural guidance for written arguments, personal interviews and handling of additional searches and rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination and reconsideration procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for reexamination, reconsideration by examiners before appeal, requirements/grounds for reconsideration and review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how applicants can seek reexamination and internal review prior to formal appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special application types: divisional, converted, and priority-claim applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements, procedures, effects and examination considerations for divisional applications, converted applications, and applications claiming priority under treaty or domestically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers requirements for filing, effects on priority and scope, and related examination instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term extension and special term extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and eligibility for patent term extension (e.g., for regulatory approval delays), period allowed, application procedure, and examination of extension requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes what subject matter is eligible and the documentation needed for term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination eligibility and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of expedited examination, objects eligible for expedited processing and guidelines for determining expedited examination by subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists eligible categories and examiner guidance for granting expedited status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio amendment, pre-amendment communication and preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on positive examination practices including suggesting amendments, ex-officio amendment procedures, pre-amendment communication interviews, preliminary examination and their follow-up processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of inappropriate suggestions of amendment and notes on ex-officio amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective examination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and process for collective examination where multiple examiners or units review an application collectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes when collective examination is used, details of the process and examiner responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria by technology (tech-specific requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology-specific examination criteria and disclosure requirements for fields such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, food, functional drinking water, chemical compounds, alloys, polymers, textiles, architectural design, and computer-related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each technology chapter provides requirements for the description/claims and for patentability specific to the technology; e.g., nucleic acid/amino acid sequences, deposit requirements for biological material, and special considerations for computer-related inventions.
